name: CoreAppSidebar

variantIntent.list: Default — flat groups, ruled apart, all open. Every existing consumer.
variantIntent.tree: Grouped sections — icon groups render as a tree, rules drop, sections open folded.

intent: The standard Core product sidebar: branded shell with a pinned block of shell surfaces (Search, a `pinnedTop` entry, Home, Notifications) over grouped nav, plus profile, density, and collapse to an icon rail with sub-tab flyouts. Search is a ROW that hands off to a search surface of the consumer's choosing, not an inline filter. Groups are navigable in their own right: give a group an `icon` and it renders as a tree — parent-sized header, a spine down to the last item, an elbow into each — and folds in the collapsed rail to that one icon, whose flyout lists its items using the same flyout an `expandable` item's `subMenu` gets. `collapsible` makes the WHOLE header fold the group — name, icon and chevron are one control, so no group name is a link and none underlines — while `activeGroupId` marks a group (and its rail icon) as the active surface and `onGroupSelect` fires only from the collapsed rail's flyout title. `variant` names the two shapes — `"list"` (default) for the flat, ruled, all-open list and `"tree"` for grouped sections that fold to their icon — and supplies the defaults for `showGroupDividers` and `groupsCollapsedByDefault`, both of which still override it. `brandName`, `showHomeDivider`, `dividerBefore` and `showSearch` tune the chrome independently of the variant; expanding and folding animate.
when: Any standard Core product app shell
A sidebar whose GROUPS are destinations too, not just headings over a list
A nav that must stay legible collapsed — one icon per section, its items in a flyout
A long nav that should open as a short list of section headers and expand on demand

chooseOver.because: The Sidebar primitive when you must build a bespoke nav; CoreAppSidebar for the standard shell

chooseOver.component: Hand-rolled grouped nav in a template
chooseOver.because: Group icons, tree spines, fold chevrons, clickable group names and the collapsed-rail flyouts all live here, so every template gets the same behaviour from props rather than reimplementing it locally.

commonMistakes.fix: Pass activeItemId to control the highlight from your route
commonMistakes.avoidOverride: Drive selection via DOM clicks — pass activeItemId to control the highlight from your route

usage: Use CoreAppSidebar to help users navigate through your application or content hierarchy. This component provides clear wayfinding and helps users understand their current location within the interface.

CoreAppSidebar is ideal for multi-page applications, content-heavy interfaces, or any situation where users need to move between different sections. Keep navigation patterns consistent across your application for better user experience.
